name: Quickstep
tagline: UW-Madison's single-node, in-memory analytical SQL engine; retired from the Apache Incubator in 2018.
description: Quickstep is a research database engine from Jignesh Patel's group at the University of Wisconsin-Madison that set out to 'scale in' rather than out: squeeze every core and byte of memory in one large server before reaching for a cluster. It decouples data flow from control flow so many work orders from many queries run in parallel, uses template metaprogramming for vectorised operators, and mixes row and column storage blocks. It entered the Apache Incubator in 2016 and retired in December 2018; the UW repository still receives occasional build fixes, most recently in 2024, but no feature work. It is useful as a readable modern analytical engine for study, not as a product.
statusNote: Apache Incubator podling retired on 2018-12-01; the UW repository gets only occasional build fixes (latest 2024). Use DuckDB for single-node analytics.

scale.notes: Targets one many-core server with large memory; spills to disk if data exceeds RAM.

strengths: Work-order scheduler decouples control flow from data flow for high intra- and inter-query parallelism
Vectorised operators generated with C++ template metaprogramming
Hybrid row/column storage blocks with compression and bitmap indexes
Permissively licensed, compact codebase for teaching analytical engine design
weaknesses: Small SQL surface; many standard features missing
No active development, releases or community since 2018
useCases: Research baselines for single-node OLAP experiments
notIdealFor: Users who need a maintained engine
